title: A leaf becomes food
hook: Compare the effects on both participants.

knows: Ecological interactions can affect participants differently.
doesNotKnow: The herbivore benefits and the plant is harmed in the stipulated case. Herbivory is a form of consumption with effects that depend on context.

misconception: An interaction must affect both participants in the same way.
objective: Classify the stated effects of an ecological interaction.

claims.text: Question, diagram and reveal: A caterpillar eats a leaf, gaining food while the plant loses tissue and is harmed in this example. Using + for benefit, − for harm and 0 for no appreciable effect, which signs describe Caterpillar and Plant, in that order? Caterpillar: +; Plant: −. The herbivore benefits and the plant is harmed in the stipulated case. Herbivory is a form of consumption with effects that depend on context.
claims.source: Stipulated simplified example; ecological definitions: OpenStax https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/45-6-community-ecology

claims.text: Icons and signs summarize the stipulated interaction and do not quantify fitness or capture every ecological effect.

Recall: What term describes the Caterpillar–Plant interaction as stated in the lesson? The herbivore benefits and the plant is harmed in the stipulated case. Herbivory is a form of consumption with effects that depend on context.
